recipes.name: Sausage, Peppers, Onions, and Potato Bake
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds Italian sausage links, cut into 2-inch pieces
4 large potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced
2 large green bell peppers, seeded and cut into wedges
2 large red bell peppers, seeded and cut into wedges
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Heat 2 teaspoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, and cook and stir the sausage until browned, 5 to 10 minutes. Transfer cooked sausage to a large baking dish.
Pour 1/4 cup of olive oil into the skillet, and cook potatoes, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 10 minutes.
Place the potatoes into the baking dish, leaving some oil in the skillet.
Cook and stir green and red peppers and onions in the hot skillet until they are beginning to soften, about 5 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the baking dish. Pour wine and chicken stock over the vegetables and sausage, and sprinkle with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Gently stir sausage, potatoes, and vegetables together.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot and bubbling, 20 to 25 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage, Peppers, Onions, and Potato Bake
raw_recipe.description: Sausage and potatoes are a classic combination. Combined with peppers, onion, and white wine, this easy Italian bake always delivers.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make a delicious meal out of sausages, peppers, onion, and potatoes. We cook each ingredient separately at first, to ensure their proper doneness. Then, we add them to a baking dish, together with a little bit of wine and chicken stock and roast in the oven until hot and bubbly. Enjoy with a green salad and a glass of wine.

review.reviewBody: This was PHENOMINAL!!! One of the best recipes that I have tried from this site, hands down. Super simple to put together and the flavor was just awesome. I made this exactly as written aside from omitting the red peppers because I didn't have any and adding in a few cloves of whole garlic. I used hot Italian sausage. My little guy wiped his plate clean, and so did we, lol! This is a definate 10 star recipe that I will be making VERY OFTEN! Thanks for sharing. :)

Very tasty. I did halve the recipe since there's only my husband and myself here and also only used chicken stock since I didn't have any white wine. It was very delicious, colorful with the peppers, etc. and smelled great while it was baking. Thanks for the recipe, Beccabo73.

The minute I saw Christina's photo and read her review of this recipe, I new we would love it. Wow! It is excellent!! Followed the recipe with the exception of using 1 each of green, red, yellow and orange peppers and threw in a couple of carrots I needed to use up. I also did not peel the new red potatoes. A couple of the kids and I don't usually care for spicey (hot), so I used 1 pound of sweet itialian and 1 pound of hot italian sausage. This was the perfect blend for us. I also threw in a little fresh thyme and fresh parsley right before putting it in the oven. It did take apporox. 40 min in my oven. This is definately a recipe that will be a reapeat here. Everyone loved it and said they are looking forward to having it again soon. Thanks for sharing!!

Delicious! I put my own spin on it. Cut everything down to half. Instead of wine I used beer(Im so used to it with sausage and was too lazy to get a bottle of wine :P ) and i doubled the chicken stock. I also added cajun seasoning and garlic salt as well as about 4 cloves of garlic. it was delicious! the potatoes came out PERFECT and very soft, the sausage had great flavor. im not even a big pepper fan but i absolutely loved them this time around. will DEFINITELY make this again!

OUTRAGEOUS! I can't wait to make this for company. I cut the recipe ingredients to 4 servings except for liquid - kept that at 8 as others suggested. I did not have chicken broth so I used all wine. Commenters said it lacked flavor so I seasoned everything (except sausage) liberally with Goya seasoning and Italian herbs before sauteing them. The potatoes were perfect (I was skeptical). I put a lid on the peppers and onions which helped to soften them quickly. I cannot tell you how good and flavorful this came out. There were only 2 of us and we ate almost the entire dish ourselves. I'm eating the leftovers-not sharing! :) Thank you submitter.
Deglaze the pan with the wine & broth and scrape up all the "bits" ... then add to baking dish. Thanks Beccabo ..... AWESOME ! The smells remind me of the sausage vendors outside of Fenway Park ! :)

Very tasty recipe, I made it as written. But, this dish takes a long time to prep and bake. I tried to make it easier by using a Le Crueset cast iron round casserole. That allowed me to cook and bake in the same pan. And cast iron skillet would work. I cooked the sausage, then removed it to a plate. Then I cooked the onions and removed from pan. I used splashes of broth to saute vegetables to reduce the amount of oil used. Then I layered thinly sliced potatoes and sprinkled with onion powder, cracked black pepper and salt. I added splashes of broth as needed to cook potatoes. I removed potatoes and sauted bell pepper slices and mushrooms next. Next, I put the potatoes, onions and lastly the cooked sausage back into the cast iron pan. I added some Italian seasoning the chicken broth and a little more salt and stirred. I put it in the oven to finish. You can cover it if the potatoes seem underdone. It was very tasty and my husband loved it. But it was a long prep time, so next time I think I would microwave the potatoes for a few minutes to speed up the cooking time.

I have made this several times. The last few times, I skipped the the skillet part, just put everything in the baking pan (food, then sprinkled with seasoning and then poured the broth -or broth and wine- over the top). I baked it for about 35 minutes and it was done. I cubed the potatoes instead of slicing them. I add a little smoked paprika like someone else suggested. I guess it may not get the added flavor from the skillet, but it saved prep time, one less thing to wash and we still enjoy this recipe.

Great recipe! I put the potatoes in the oven while the sausage was browning and then removed them. Using the juices in the pan, I browned the green peppers and onions, adding dry basil, red pepper flakes, and garlic (when nearly done). Sliced the sausage and placed on top of potatoes, added the peppers and onions on top and baked at 400 for 40 minutes. It was delicious! Thanks for sharing. It will be on my rotation, to be sure.

This was so delicious, my hubby said, if I continue to make meals this good, we'll never eat out again. I did make a few changes just to reduce my prep time and make it a one pot meal. Instead of browning anything on top of the stove, I placed everything in a oven pan... hot ital sausage, frozen mixed peppers and onion, garlic, drained can potatoes, wine, broth and seasoning in 400 degree oven for 1 hour. I turned sausage over after 1/2 hour once top browned, then turned again twice after each 15 minutes. I also browned sausage for an additional 2 min under broiler before removing. I've made it both ways, but I prefer this way more. It's quicker, less prep and more flavorful to me and hubby.

This is a family favourite! I found this a couple years ago and it has been a hit with all who try it! I don’t like to fry everything so I bake the sausage and soften the potatoes in a steamer instead. Healthier and takes a lot of the work out of it as well. We also use spicy sausage as it gives the dish a massive kick(we love spicy). Seriously best sausage recipe and I’m sure my family will be eating it for generations.
It is much faster to fry everything jn a frying pan.
One of the best recipes I've ever made. I thought the potatoes was a strange addition but they work so well with the other ingredients. Made exactly as written

Made this for the first time last night, using Johnsonville mild Italian sausage. I used canned sliced potatoes to save some time and avoid the "fun" of peeling. I also used a red onion along with a couple yellow. The color of the red onion did bleed a bit onto some of the potatoes, and of course they have a little stronger onion flavor, but it worked fine. The dish came together pretty much as the recipe describes, though my stovetop cook times were a little longer than the times listed. I made the standard size, with two pounds of sausage (actually two packages, 19 ounces each, so it was a little closer to two and a half pounds), and wow this makes a lot of food! But it's delicious - lots of flavor and great veggies.

Made half the recipe. Browned the sausages whole and seasoned vegetables with half packet of Italian dressing mix and a splash of marsala. Plan to stir leftovers into a prepared box of Pasa-Roni and bake in the oven.

I used kielbasa sausage instead of Italian sausage, and swapped the Italian seasoning for garlic and Ancho chili powder. I also left out the white wine using only the 1/2 cup of chicken stock. I feel like one cup of liquid would have been too much. My husband and I enjoyed this for dinner. He said this dish was delicious! I made cornbread as a side dish and it paired well.

This recipe has a number of problems. There is no direction for adding wine and stock. When reducing to 1/2 recipe not all ingredients are adjusted in the direction section. Contradiction of thick or thin sliced potatoes. However, if you make the necessary adjustments, the meal is excellent.

I haven't made with potatoes, but I just place sausage, peppers & onions on a cookie sheet without frying anything! I season with salt, pepper and garlic powder and drizzle with olive oil. Why dirty another pan frying when it's not necessary?
I have been making this recipe for years and everybody loves it. Give it a try!

This is such a classic! I recall an elderly Italian couple who had a version of this every Sunday the way non-Italians serve roast beef for Sunday dinner. My friends would add carrots, too. I am grateful that you provided the recipe because I never got one from her. I've tried making it over the years but I can see that my efforts would have been improved with 3 things that you suggest: 1) Browning the sausage first, 2) Pre-cooking the potatoes, and 3) Adding white wine.
